text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- U.S. President Bill Clinton wins decisive victory but triumph lessened by re-election of a Republican Congress.
- Clinton's re-election will mean continuity and stability in American foreign policy, a Singapore Foreign Ministry spokesman says.
- Asian financial markets move higher after Clinton presidential win and Republican congressional victory.

- Two days after side-stepping questions on his political aspirations, Indonesian Research and Technology Minister B.J. Habibie suggets Indonesia's next vice-president should be someone who could share President Suharto's responsibilities so he could enjoy his old age.
- Suntec City retail complex teams up with neighbouring rivals Millenia Singapore and Marina Square to draw in crowds and beat tough retail market.
- Government's prediction of two percent fourth quarter growth in gross domestic product is conservative, Minister for Trade and Industry Yeo Cheow Tong says.
- Asia/Pacific to lead US$1.2 trillion electronics market.
- It would be unsatisfactory for there to be dual proceedings with inconsistent findings against auditors of Baring Futures (Singapore), judge says in ongoing hearings.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Singapore property tycoon Ng Teng Fong's Sino Hotels to pay about Hong Kong $1.1 billion for 50 percent stake in five-star Conrad Hotel in Hong Kong.
- Financial markets give thumbs-up to U.S. election results.
- Economists surprised by poor economic outlook for fourth quarter pointing to 1.9 percent growth.
- Avimo Group says shutdown of Penang plant and relocation to Singapore have nothing to do with projects related to Singapore Armed Forces.
- Nobel Design holdings expected to raise about S$7 million in initial public offering this week.
- Mainboard-listed Cam International Holdings pulls out of troubled gaming venture in Fiji to concentrate on projects nearer home.
- Mainboard-listed Singtronics group makes first move into hotel development in Australia.
- Singapore Aircraft Leasing Enterprise (Sale) orders V2500 engines from International Aero Engines for recent order of 24 aircraft from Airbus.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
